editorial.headline: Coconut Coir Fiber, Nationally Open but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 32905 covers industrial processing of coconut husk into coir materials, with all business scales open nationally but PMA registration blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 32905 is a narrow but important industrial activity: the processing of coconut husk into raw materials. The record identifies three outputs at the center of the scope: coconut coir fiber, or cocofiber; coconut coir powder, or cocopeat; and rubberized curl coir, known in the Indonesian text as serat sabut kelapa berkaret or sebutret. This is not the retailing of coconut products or the cultivation of coconuts. It is the conversion of husk into industrial material.

The business-scale picture is unusually broad. The slim record marks the activity as open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators. In practical registration terms, that means the classification is not reserved only for large factories or only for small household-level activity. It can describe a small processor as well as a larger industrial setup, as long as the registered activity remains within the stated processing scope: coconut husk transformed into cocofiber, cocopeat, or rubberized coir.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling in the record is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. On the national layer, then, this is a foreign-open activity with no lower percentage cap appearing in the slim record. That matters, because it means any restriction in this draft cannot be invented from the nature of the product, the location, or an assumed local-partner rule. The only national ownership number here is the 100% figure.

Bali changes the outcome. The record marks this activity as blocked for Bali PMA registration, with the Bali status Blocked (risk class). The stated reason is that the OSS risk at Besar scale is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, bringing it under the Bali moratorium that blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the island. So the honest conclusion is simple: nationally, KBLI 32905 is open to foreign ownership; in Bali, a foreigner cannot register it today because the Bali-side block applies. There is no Bali percentage cap in the record, and no separate Bali quota or partnership condition to describe. The restriction is a registration block, not a reduced foreign-ownership ceiling.
